name: avatar
title: Avatar
description: User portraits shown as clipped circles, with a grey initials fallback when a picture is unavailable, plus an overlapping stack of smaller faces that ends in a plus-eight counter.
use: You show people by face and need a tidy fallback when a photo is missing or fails.
avoid: Falls back to dull initials, and the demo pulls images from an external placeholder service.
a11y: Images carry alt text in the demo and fallbacks show initials; the decorative stack images are given an empty alt. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two rows on black. The top row has six large round portraits: four photos, a grey circle reading JL and a softened-square portrait. Below, five small round photos overlap and end in a grey circle reading +8.
behaves: Static: nothing moves. Photos simply fill their circles, and a missing or failed image would swap to initials on a flat grey circle.
customise: You supply the image and the fallback as children; size and corner radius come from className, and the fallback text is whatever you put inside it.
weight: light: Remote images clipped to a circle; no animation or script beyond image loading.
demo: Portrait photos of named people, a grey JL fallback, a square-cornered portrait and a stacked group ending in +8.
issues: The square portrait and grey JL circle sit in a row of round faces, which reads as accidental
Every frame is the same, so loading and fallback states are never actually shown
polishWhy: Neat photo set with a working initials fallback; the mixed round and square shapes clash.
